definitions.explanation: Being completely focused on one thing without any distraction; concentrating with one's entire heart and mind.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{一心不乱|いっしんふらん}に{勉強|べんきょう}した。
{一心不乱|いっしんふらん}に{仕事|しごと}に{打|う}ち{込|こ}む。
examples.english: To throw oneself wholeheartedly into work.

examples.japanese: {一心不乱|いっしんふらん}に{走|はし}り{続|つづ}けた。
examples.english: I kept running with complete focus.

notes:
FOUR-CHARACTER IDIOM ({四字熟語|よじじゅくご}):
{一心|いっしん} (one mind) + {不乱|ふらん} (not distracted)
Literally: "one mind, not scattered"

ORIGIN:
Originally a Buddhist term describing a meditative state of complete concentration.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {一心不乱|いっしんふらん}に{取|と}り{組|く}む: to work on wholeheartedly
- {一心不乱|いっしんふらん}に{打|う}ち{込|こ}む: to devote oneself to
- {一心不乱|いっしんふらん}に{努力|どりょく}する: to make efforts wholeheartedly

SIMILAR EXPRESSIONS:
- {無我夢中|むがむちゅう}: being absorbed in
- {一途|いちず}に: single-mindedly
